text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- German luxury car maker BMW has doubled purchases of car parts from Norway during the last five years. BMW is buying car parts worth 256 million crowns from Norway this year and may increase business further.

- Today the first delivery of natural gas from the Troll shelf begins officially. The Troll agreement is Norway's biggest export agreement ever. Norway will deliver gas worth an estimated 700 billion crowns to continental Europe.

- Norway's Varner Group today becomes the first Scandinavian textile company to open its first three stores in Gdynia, Poland. Varner has invested 12-15 million crowns in Poland and is expecting 40 million crowns in turnover this year. Varner has stores in Iceland, Lithuania and Sweden.
-- Aker and RGI have resumed merger talks, which were called off on Monday.

- Morgan Stanley has downgraded the EPS forecast for Norwegian forestry group Norske Skogindustrier for 1996 by 2.44 percent to 29.98 crowns. The broker firm lowered profits forecasts for the whole forestry sector in early September.
- Mo i Rana in northern Norway and Fredrikstad in southeast Norway will get the country's first duty-free ports for the import, production and export of commodities.
